newsitem.title: FRANCE: Britain made BSE mistakes, Tory Euro MP says.
newsitem.headline: Britain made BSE mistakes, Tory Euro MP says.

text.p: The British government made mistakes in the way it handled the mad cow crisis, a leading British Conservative member of the European Parliament said on Tuesday.
But he criticised fellow Euro-MPs for condemning Britain.
"Whilst mistakes were made and people have said we could have done better in the past...I don't think that calls for condemnation," Lord Plumb, himself a dairy farmer, told a news conference.

He said the Conservative British government's announcement last March that there could be links between bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) and the human brain disease Creutzfeldt- Jakob Disease was "unfortunate".

On Wednesday the European assembly is due to approve a scathing report drafted by the parliament's committee of inquiry into the handling of the crisis in the beef industry which followed the announcement.
The parliament was also expected to pass a resolution threatening to sack the Commission unless it carries out the report's demands for reform by December.
But Plumb made it clear he would support neither move and attacked the report for criticising Britain.
"I think what the general public want to hear is not who did what...but whether British beef is safe to eat," he said.
